TESTIMONY IN SUPPORT OF:
LD 864 "An Act to Allow the Use of Transporter Plates for Transporting Campers or Motor Homes"
THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE TRANSPORTATION
SPONSORED BY: Representative Cray from Palmyra
Good afternoon, Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation. I am Representative Dean Cray representing Canaan, Detroit, Hartland, St. Albans, and Palmyra. I am here today to introduce a constituent bill LD 864, "An Act to Allow the Use of Transporter Plates for Transporting Campers or Motor Homes."
The intent of this bill is to allow the movement of campers and motorhomes for the purpose
selling and repairing using transport plates. Transport plates are currently used for the moving
of heavy trailers but does not allow for the moving of travel trailers or motorhomes. To move
such things requires an individual to go to the municipality to get a plate for each unit. This
means if one were to bring three campers to a shop for repair in the same day, currently you would have to go to the town office and acquire three separate plates even if you had a
transport plate for heavy trailers.
I have testimony from Steven Philbrick who is the constituent who requested this bill for you to
read. He could not be here today because he is working but I would appreciate you taking the time to familiarize his testimony. I will try and answer any questions and will be here for the work session.
Thank you for your time.
Sincerely,

Dean A. Cray
State Representative

JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORTATION
L.D. 864 66An Act to Allow the Use of Transporter Plates for Transporting Campers or Motor Homes"
Testimony of Shenna Bellows, Secretary of State and Cathie Curtis, Deputy Secretary for the Bureau of Motor Vehicles,
Department of the Secretary of State
March 27, 2025

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and distinguished members of the Transportation Committee, I
am speaking in opposition to L.D. 864 "An Act to Allow the Use of Transporter Plates for Transporting
Campers or Motor Homes" .
The bill seeks to amend the criteria for obtaining a Transporter license plate, to allow businesses that sell or service camp trailers or motor homes to qualify to use the plate and charge a fee for the movement of the trailer or motor home.
The purpose of a transporter plate is to allow entities to move a vehicle that is in their possession temporarily because it is being towed, repossessed, recycled, or moved to a location to sell.
Under current law, a business that is properly licensed to sell camp trailers and motor homes are issued dealer plates to move them. Therefore, this amendment is not necessary for licensed dealers. However, current law does not allow businesses that only service the vehicles to use Transporter plates. The reason for this is that the owners of the camp trailers and motor homes are required to register them, making a
transporter plate umrecessary once the vehicle is sold.
This amendment would provide a mechanism for moving the vehicles to campgrounds or seasonal lots without the owner registering or titling them. Thereby they could avoid paying the excise tax owed to their municipalities and the registration and title fees owed to the state highway fund. It could also provide a mechanism for an unlicensed seller to move a vehicle without being properly licensed.
In summary, there are valid reasons for businesses to have Transporter Plates, but we believe the current
law adequately address these needs and to expand the use provides an opportunity to circumvent the
vehicle registration laws. For this reason, we urge the committee to vote unanimously ought not to pass.
